title: Adaptive batch/cache autotuner with golden-prompt regression gates
creator: Anika Patel
description: Implement an adaptive autotuner that recommends and safely applies batching and KV-cache configurations per model/route to reduce token cost while enforcing quality safeguards. This ticket covers: 1) telemetry collection and heuristics to infer optimal batch sizes and cache policies per workload; 2) a staged apply mechanism that can do dry-run, shadow-canary, and holdback comparisons; 3) automated quality gating based on a compact eval suite anchored by golden prompts and micro-evals; and 4) safe rollback/upfront rollback recommendations when degradations exceed acceptance thresholds. The goal is to enable non-intrusive cost reductions (20-40% per-token cost in target workloads) without measurable quality regressions for critical prompt families. Non-goals: model architecture changes, heavy-weight offline training, or replacing manual approvals for high-risk customers.
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner produces per-route batching and KV-cache recommendations with expected cost delta estimate and confidence score
Staged apply flow: dry-run -> shadow-canary (10% mirrored traffic) -> progressive rollouts with automatic holdback if guards fail
Eval suite implemented: 150 golden prompts + 50 adversarial variants + automated reference scoring for the top-3 quality metrics
Pass/fail gating enforced: no more than 1% absolute drop in golden-prompt pass-rate or 0.5-point BLEU/ROUGE equivalent across targeted prompts
Rollback triggered automatically when regression exceeds thresholds; rollback completes within configured SLA (<= 5 minutes to revert route config)
Dashboard surfaces recommendation rationale, confidence, and per-prompt diffs; telemetry links to PR and rollout history
End-to-end test coverage for the staged apply and rollback paths and an integration test in the canary cluster
notes_and_updates: 2026-02-15: Kickoff meeting — arrived at scope and initial heuristics. Action: prototype telemetry pipeline. (notes drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/autotuner-kickoff)

2026-02-22: Prototype telemetry agent submitted. Agent captures per-request seq_len, kv-hit-ratio, latency-percentiles, and per-route token cost. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3987

2026-03-01: Design review with PM and DX — agreed on 'golden prompt leash' gating model and that thresholds default to conservative values (1% pass-rate drop). Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/Autotuner-Gating

2026-03-05: Built first evaluation harness (nodejs) that runs golden prompts against baseline and candidate configs and computes delta metrics. Test harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/102

2026-03-08: Experiment: Shadow-canary on internal traffic for route 'chat-completion-standard' - observed 28% cost reduction predicted; however, two prompts in the golden set showed a 2.3% pass-rate drop. Decision: hold rollout and refine batching heuristic to preserve ordering-sensitive prompts.
2026-03-11: Trade-off session — added prompt fingerprinting to force conservative caching for read-heavy, few-shot prompts. Action: update heuristics and rerun shadow-canary.
2026-03-12: Security reviewed telemetry fields (PII redaction OK). Security ticket: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/issues/214
implementation_steps: 1) Instrument per-route telemetry and centralize into cost-optimizer index
2) Implement heuristics service that suggests batch_size and cache_policy with a confidence score
3) Add staged apply API: dry-run, shadow, progressive, rollback endpoints
4) Build compact eval suite and scoring pipeline (golden prompts + micro-evals + adversarial variants)
5) Integrate gating logic to block rollouts and surface human-review when thresholds breached
6) Add dashboards and alerting for autotuner recommendations and live diffs
7) End-to-end tests and runbook for manual override and incident response
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): unit tests + integration in staging cluster; run against synthetic traffic
Phase 1 (shadow-canary): mirror 10% production traffic, generate reports daily; manual review required for any regression > 0.5%
Phase 2 (gradual rollout): 5% -> 20% -> 50% with automated gates at each step; monitor golden-prompt pass-rate and latency P99
Phase 3 (default): enable recommendations for low-risk routes and surface opt-in for high-risk routes; provide one-click rollback in console
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive batching increases tail latency and causes timeouts. Mitigation: cap batch sizes per-route based on P99 latency budget and add backpressure signals.
Risk: Golden prompt set not comprehensive leading to missed regressions. Mitigation: continuous enrichment of golden set via traffic-sampling and customer-provided prompts.
Risk: False positives during A/B because traffic distribution changes. Mitigation: use paired statistical tests and maintain control windows for at least 24 hours.
Risk: Rollback fails due to state drift. Mitigation: ensure idempotent config apply and store previous configs as immutable snapshots for fast revert.
